data.narrative:
Mainspring Energy, a Series F climate and energy company founded by Shannon Miller, Adam Simpson, and Matt Svrcek, has raised $650M+ to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, though narrow same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables remain sparse; top private peers include Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method, using total capital raised ($650M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 1.3x step-up multiplier from Series F to the next funding round, yielding $845M. A peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage datapoints within the Climate & Energy sector; only one narrowly comparable company at Series F existed, below the three-company threshold required for reliable median-based triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $718M (low) to $972M (high), centered on $845M. This range reflects the mechanical application of stage-progression logic absent corroborating peer benchmarks. Key uncertainties include the absence of tightly comparable Series F or Series G transactions in the frontier energy space, the reliance on total capital raised as a valuation proxy rather than market-driven pricing, and nascent public market data in this sector. A subsequent funding round or M&A event would provide stronger pricing signals.
